name: Conservative liberalism
summary: Conservative liberalism, as the scholarship that uses the name describes it, is a liberalism of ordered liberty under God and the law. It draws on classical philosophy, Christianity and ancient institutions such as common law, rather than on Locke, Kant or Mill, and rejects the autonomy of the human will, blind faith in progress and the utopian ideologies that lead to totalitarianism. Its main thinker is Tocqueville.
scope: The tradition Mahoney and Kraynak call conservative liberalism, centred on Tocqueville (and, in those sources, de Jouvenel, Aron and others), with Tocqueville's own texts as its primary sources. It excludes liberal conservatism, ordoliberalism and party practice, which the defining sources do not tie to the name.

At its practical best, conservative liberalism promotes ordered liberty under God and establishes constitutional safeguards against tyranny.
